assumptions: The Program emits 1-TM-score constraints; raw TM-score is recovered as 1 minus the stored score.
Adenylate kinase is a representative example in the paper, but this collection is one target-level protocol slice rather than the full 86-protein benchmark.
The 50 full variants encode the Table 1 allocation exactly for one target: ten beta settings times five seeds times five draws equals 250 models per method.
The paper reports five seeds but not their values; implementation seeds 0 through 4 are paired identically across full and fused arms.
Only backends explicitly registered through register_reviewed_pair_scaling_backend may execute; absence raises an error instead of silently running beta zero.
The reduced smoke variant exercises the audited Boltz-2 path only; full variants retain both paper predictors.
unknowns: The Boltz-2 2.2.1 backend is independently implemented as an audited Pairformer pre-hook that rejects a run unless it fires once per trunk pass. The AlphaFold3 backend remains unavailable and fails closed because licensed weights are not present.
The collection encodes one adenylate-kinase protocol slice, not the complete 86-target benchmark.
Per-state Cα RMSD success, worst-case RMSD, best-minimum TM-score, and fill ratio remain ensemble-level collection analysis beyond the per-model TM-score constraints.
